description: FILED s532 (Fable 5.1, 2026-11-02) from the round board run on MAIN-READY-63 b31345ca (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s532/review/board-main63.rows.tsv): NEW rows Template-Toolkit compile2.t #1 #2 (unnamed) + *PLAN* "ran 5 of 9", compile5.t *PLAN* "ran 3 of 3, rc 2" + rows 1-3 "cached foo / bar / blam"; s531a had already noted that compile2.t / compile5.t depend on compile1.t / compile4.t running FIRST (its rows were measured by one-file runs in order on the combined tree, docs/session-log.md "Rebases and the register").  MECHANISM: tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl builds @work from every dist's sorted t/ listing and spawns `shift @queue` onto $jobs workers (lines ~277-414): compile2.t starts while compile1.t is still writing t/test/src/*.ttc (and compile5.t before compile4.t) -- perl's `make test` runs a dist's files in sequence, so the dist relies on it.  The blessed rows for compile2/compile5 are therefore ORDER-DEPENDENT in a whole-board run and the board's --diff cannot tell an order artifact from a regression.  FIX SHAPE (tools layer, task #1502's instrument): a per-dist flag in baselines/cpan-board-dists.tsv (`--serial`: the dist's files run one at a time in sorted order on ONE worker while other dists fill the other workers) -- or a dependency column `after=FILE` per file in baselines/cpan-board-timeouts.tsv's sibling registry; measure the board's wall time BEFORE -> AFTER (TT has 121 files, most under 5 s).  Until then: the TT compile rows are verified by one-file runs in order (compile1..5 in ONE run-dist-t.pl invocation or sequentially), never from a whole-board run; the s532 round's compile2/compile5 NEW rows are NOT blessed (artifact).  Layer: tools.  Queued: s532b (tools member).
subject: The CPAN board runs a dist's t-files from one sorted queue on 4-8 workers, so a file that depends on an EARLIER file's side effect races it: Template-Toolkit compile2.t / compile5.t read the .ttc cache compile1.t / compile4.t write, and read FAIL / extra NEW rows in a whole-board run while a one-file run in order passes -- the board needs a per-dist serial (or ordered-dependency) rule
